title: Implementing Microsoft Purview — Foundation, Roles & Onboarding
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Microsoft Purview implementation).

Microsoft Purview portal / Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph authored at exact detail from Microsoft public docs; Purview features are heavily licensing-/plan-dependent (E5 / E5 Compliance; some preview) and the portal is evolving — availability + paths cited or flagged 'verify your licensing/tenant', never invented. Regulatory/records/legal determinations (retention schedules, file plans, legal holds, insider-risk case actions) deferred to compliance/records/privacy/legal — solutions give the technical method + evidence, not the determination; policies piloted in simulation/test before enforcement. Automation is PowerShell (S&C PowerShell / Graph); no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Stand up Microsoft Purview the right way — foundation, roles, and onboarding
problem: Microsoft Purview is powerful and sprawling — and most orgs turn on pieces ad hoc without a foundation. This solution implements Purview properly: enable and organize the Purview portal, establish the role groups and RBAC (least-privilege for compliance/records/insider-risk/eDiscovery/audit), turn on the core data services (Content & Activity Explorer, unified audit), baseline Compliance Manager, connect the in-scope workloads, and set the operating foundation the rest of the Purview capabilities build on.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the Purview portal and capability map, the role/RBAC model, the core data services (Content/Activity Explorer, audit), Compliance Manager, and the phased-adoption approach.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (compliance licensing E3/E5, admin roles, in-scope workloads, stakeholders).

Implementation Guide — organize the portal, establish role groups + least-privilege RBAC, enable Content/Activity Explorer + unified audit, baseline Compliance Manager, connect workloads, and validate the foundation — pilot-first, each role/scope named.

5 PowerShell scripts — Discovery, Configuration/Remediation, Validation, Reporting, and a scope/health helper — authentic Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph automation (read-only or -WhatIf by default; no credentials in code).
Validation gates (roles scoped, data services on, Compliance Manager baselined) plus Best Practices + a capability-adoption roadmap; licensing dependencies flagged to verify.
short: Implement Microsoft Purview properly — the portal, least-privilege role/RBAC model, core data services (Content/Activity Explorer, unified audit), Compliance Manager baseline, and workload connections — the foundation the rest of Purview builds on. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
